rationale: This is a one-knob strictness tweak (three-year mean accrual → three-year max) applied to AccrualQualityOffBalanceSheetCapital, leaving both legs, coverage and economic content essentially unchanged, so it is a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism.

The confound it targets (hidden-capital-to-equity being high because equity is thin) is a real and worthwhile diagnostic, but the implementation is a third MIN leg drawn entirely from already-tested archive components and is very close to MatureIntangibleStockCredibility/MagnitudeAndCredibilityInvisibleCapital, so it adds little beyond an incremental intersection.

Genuinely novel in that it exploits the archive's documented sign reversal between self-built and purchased intangible capital by differencing two nonlinear conjunctions rather than two raw characteristics, though the reviewer should note that COALESCE(intan,0) creates a large tie mass at zero so the long tail mixes credible organic innovators with firms that simply have no purchased intangibles.

The fiscal channel is a legitimately new conditioning dimension for this archive, but ib/pi is sign-unstable whenever pretax income is near zero or negative (the cash-profitability gate does not guarantee pi>0), so high ranks will include loss-adjacent firms rather than genuinely tax-favored ones, and the underlying low-effective-tax-rate return effect is already a published anomaly.

A defensible sample-extension/robustness test that holds the intangible leg fixed and would meaningfully raise confidence if alpha survives at higher coverage, but it is a profitability-proxy swap that abandons the accrual-credibility mechanism (ib+dp is not cash-backed earnings), so a positive result would speak to the profitability leg's generality more than to the stated mechanism.

Flipping one leg from IND_RANK to RANK is a mechanical neutralization ablation whose likely outcome — loading on a few intangible-heavy industries with unstable portfolio composition — is well anticipated, and it does not constitute a new economic mechanism.
